notes: §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 SRL3.2 keeps the association in the 1985 language: "Associating the figurative constant ALL literal where the length of the literal is greater than one with a data item that is numeric or numeric edited is an obsolete feature in Standard COBOL." The acceptance half conforms: GateSr3 asks the registry row all-literal-multichar-numeric-removed-2002, which is silent at 85 and COBOL0902 from 2002, for every MOVE (GateMove), INITIALIZE REPLACING and relation (CheckRelationalOperands). The value half is right for an integer numeric receiver only (AllDigitFill repeats the literal over the receiver's digits): probed at --std 85, MOVE ALL "12" gives 1212, 121, 12121 and 1 for PIC 9(4), 9(3), 9(5) and 9, ALL "123" gives 1231, COMP and PACKED-DECIMAL receivers agree, and IF, EVALUATE and INITIALIZE REPLACING NUMERIC DATA agree. It is wrong for the two other receivers the rule names. A numeric edited receiver is not edited: ConvertSource returns the repeated characters as the item's image for any ALL literal whose receiver is not of category numeric, so PIC 9(3).99 holds 121212 and PIC ZZ,ZZ9 holds 121212. A noninteger numeric receiver takes the repeated digits at its own scale (AllDigitFill), so PIC 9(3)V99 holds 121.21. §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3 puts the figurative constant in category alphanumeric and GR4 b moves it "as if the sending operand were described as an unsigned numeric integer", with "alignment by decimal point" and editing; the compiler does exactly that for the nonnumeric literal of the same characters (MOVE "121212" gives 212.00, MOVE "12121" gives 121.00). A receiver with SIGN SEPARATE takes its digit count, not its "number of character positions" (PIC S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE holds +121 where the four-character string 1212 gives 212), a third case of the same mechanism. The single-character ALL literal has the same defect at 85, 2002 and 2014 (MOVE ALL "7" TO PIC 9(3).99 holds 777777). The witness moves ALL "12" to PIC 9(4) and displays 1212. No kb/Work note owns the fix.

next.reason: 1985: "ALL literal where the length of the literal is greater than one with a data item that is numeric or numeric edited is an obsolete feature"; 2023: "permitted to move an ALL "literal" figurative constant (containing only digits) ... to an integer numeric item. In all other cases ... prohibited". 1985 keeps any multi-character ALL literal with numeric or numeric-edited items as obsolete. 2023 keeps only digit-only literals moved to integer numeric items and prohibits all other cases.
